summary:
We transformed SPHEREx observations into an interactive visual experience, allowing users to explore, compare, and identify changes in the night sky over time.

Our website utilizes an evidence-based approach in supporting citizen scientists to grow the data processing capacities of this project. We use an intuitive design with supportive documents/feedback loops to assist in people using our website.
details:
Our project is an interactive website for exploring SPHEREx space telescope data. Users enter right ascension, declination, and an observation date range, and the website searches IRSA for matching observations. It then displays the available space images along with information like the detector and wavelength.

The main benefit is that it makes astronomy data easier to explore without needing to download or understand complicated FITS files manually. Our goal is to help students and other beginners learn more about space observations and make real scientific data feel more accessible.

We used Python with FastAPI for the backend and TypeScript/Next.js for the frontend. We also used Astroquery, Astropy, Matplotlib, and the IRSA SPHEREx archive. The project mainly uses software and online telescope data rather than special hardware.

Our project is creative because it turns a complicated astronomy archive into a simple interactive dashboard. While developing it, we considered ease of use, image loading speed, searching by coordinates and dates, handling large amounts of data, and making the interface understandable for people who may not have an astronomy background.
